title: Week in Ripples, Sat 31 Oct: Intel's worst day since 1974 sinks the Nasdaq
description:
Hot topic: Intel's worst day since 1974 sinks the Nasdaq 2.9% and spreads AI-spending fears across chips. Then: Reliance's record quarter, Brent at a six-month high, the Nifty's week, Amazon's capex, Bank of Baroda, Fed hike odds, Indian Oil, Sun Pharma and the rupee.

1. Nasdaq sinks 2.9% as Intel has its worst day since 1974 and AI spending fears hit chips (Reuters via Investing.com; Reuters via WHTC; TheStreet)
2. Reliance posts a record Q2 profit of Rs 29,550 crore, up 34%, on a 68% jump in refining earnings (Mint via TradingView; Whalesbook)
3. Brent hits a six-month high above $113 after a limpet-mine strike in Hormuz and Houthi missiles at Riyadh (Reuters via Press News Agency; CBS News; Gulf News)
4. Nifty rises 0.5% to 23,053 for a second gain as IT jumps 2.3% and FIIs turn buyers (5paisa; Kotak Neo; NewsBytes)
5. Amazon's AWS growth speeds up to 39%, but $220 billion of capex and negative free cash flow worry investors (StockTitan; Reuters via Investing.com)
6. Bank of Baroda's Q2 profit jumps 36% to Rs 6,532 crore as gross NPAs fall to 1.78% (Indian Masterminds; BusinessToday)
7. Fed hike odds near 80% after 3.6% PCE as the 10-year yield drops to 4.93% on the tech rout (Fox Business; Rallies.ai; Newsquawk)
8. Indian Oil's Q2 profit nearly triples to Rs 21,630 crore on refining margins (Free Press Journal)
9. Sun Pharma's Q2 profit falls 36% on a Rs 1,269 crore one-time loss; Ilumya wins a US approval (Business Standard; BusinessToday)
10. Rupee jumps 33 paise to 94.93 per dollar on a weaker dollar and RBI intervention (PTI via Whalesbook; CNBC-TV18 via TradingView)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated from the hosts' own recordings. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm Pri.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm SU. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: It's Saturday, so this is our Week in Ripples. And the big one: Intel just had its worst day since 1974.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: SU, a chip giant crashing. What happened?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Intel fell 28.6% on Friday. It guided Q4 revenue to 15 to 16 billion dollars, against 17.07 billion expected.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It blamed an explosion at its Israel fab and a slump in PCs.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And it dragged everyone down with it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nasdaq fell 2.86% to 25,437. The S&P 500 lost 1.82%, and the Dow 1.09%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who else moved?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: AMD fell 10.9%, Qualcomm 11.1%, Dell 10.8%, and Nvidia 4.2%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: For October, the Nasdaq lost 5.3%, and the Philadelphia chip index 15.4%, its worst month since March 2025.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Okay, but that's Wall Street. Why should India care about an American chip company?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. A chip-led rout sets a risk-off tone for Indian electronics makers, IT, and foreign flows on Monday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And it lands right before the US midterms on Tuesday, with Nvidia's results due on 19 November.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what do we watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The trigger is Monday's open. If US futures stay weak and Asian chip stocks fall again, the selling spreads. A quick Nvidia rebound would end it.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: Dixon, Netweb, Kaynes, and TCS. Sentiment: negative.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: Reliance has a record quarter.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Reliance's Q2 profit rose 34% to 29,550 crore rupees. EBITDA hit a record 62,409 crore, and oil-to-chemicals EBITDA jumped 67.9%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any weak spot?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Retail. Reliance Retail's profit fell 24.3% to 2,611 crore rupees. The results came after Friday's close, so the stock reacts Monday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the Nifty's second-largest stock riding war-time refining margins is direct support for the index. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Reliance, MRPL, BPCL, HPCL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: oil hits a six-month high.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: January Brent rose 2.63 dollars to settle at 113.43 dollars, after a tanker in Hormuz was hit by explosive devices and the Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And Washington?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US officials told Gulf allies to prepare for a brief but intense campaign against Iran after Tuesday's midterms. Brent rose more than 15% in October.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: India imports most of its oil, so every 10 dollars on Brent widens the trade deficit. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: ONGC, Oil India, Indian Oil, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: back home, a quietly good week.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty rose 0.51% to 23,053, about 2% up for the week. Nifty IT gained 2.32%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the foreigners finally showed up?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Provisional data show FIIs net bought 3,598 crore rupees. But they sold about 48,760 crore in October up to the 29th.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the first big FII buying day in weeks now meets a 2.9% Nasdaq fall. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Infosys, Wipro, Coforge, Trent.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: Amazon, and the cost of the AI race.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: AWS revenue grew 39% to 46.0 billion dollars. But 2026 capex is guided at about 220 billion dollars, and trailing free cash flow was minus 42.4 billion.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The stock pared an 11% after-hours fall to close down 1.4%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: faster cloud growth supports Indian IT and data centres, but the cash burn is driving the AI sell-off. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: TCS, Infosys, Anant Raj.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Bank of Baroda cleans up.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Net profit rose 35.8% to 6,532 crore rupees. Operating profit jumped 50.9%, and gross NPAs fell to 1.78% from 2.16%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: clean asset quality supports the PSU bank rally while the RBI holds rates. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Bank of Baroda, SBI, PNB, Canara Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: the Fed might actually hike.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US PCE inflation came in at 3.6% a year. CME FedWatch put December hike odds at 79.6%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Yet bond yields fell?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Yes. The 10-year fell 6.4 basis points to 4.925%, as money fled the chip sell-off into bonds.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a hiking Fed keeps the dollar firm and foreign flows into India cautious. Sentiment: negative. What to watch: US payrolls on 6 November.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: Indian Oil's profit nearly triples.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Standalone profit rose 184% to 21,630 crore rupees, from 7,610 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 30%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So all good for oil marketers?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Not quite. That quarter caught refining margins before crude went above 110 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: refining cushions state fuel retailers, but Brent above 110 now squeezes marketing margins. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Indian Oil, BPCL, HPCL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: Sun Pharma, a messy headline.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit fell 36.2% to 1,988 crore rupees after a 1,269 crore one-time loss. Revenue rose 11.9%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The US FDA approved Ilumya for psoriatic arthritis, and the stock closed up 0.95%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: US generics fell, so the specialty pipeline now carries the stock. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr Reddy's.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And story ten: the rupee gets a lift.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee closed at 94.93 per dollar, up 33 paise, as the dollar index fell 0.37%. Dealers cited RBI intervention.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee eases import costs, but 113 dollar oil limits how far it runs. Sentiment: mixed. What to watch Monday: whether it stays below 95.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch Monday: Reliance's reaction, chip stocks in Asia, and whether FIIs keep buying into Tuesday's midterms.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
